classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the hidden edges to identify and name the prism's faces, construct projections from specified directions, and redraw the wedge from another viewpoint. Preserving triangular-end connections and visibility is the hardest demand; Euler verification is direct counting and substitution.

content.prompt: A wedge-shaped solid is shown. It is drawn on isometric dot paper.

spec.sourceRegion: Review exercise Question 1, upper labelled wedge
spec.description: Six labelled vertices on staggered isometric dots. AF and BC span three horizontal intervals; BE and CD span two vertical intervals. Ordinary source colours become black; dashes retain hidden-edge meaning.
spec.mathematics: Triangular ends AEB and FDC; connecting edges AF, BC and ED. Visible edges AB, BC, CD, DF, FA and FC; hidden edges AE, EB and ED.
spec.answerVisibility: All source givens remain visible; no answers supplied.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What type of prism is this?

answer.worked: The two identical, parallel triangular end faces are $AEB$ and $FDC$, so the solid is a triangular prism.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Name the faces of this prism.

answer.worked: The triangular end faces are $BEA$ and $CDF$. The three remaining faces, named around their boundaries, are $ABCF$, $AEDF$ and $BCDE$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Draw the plan view, back view and side view of this solid. For the back view, look directly towards face $BCDE$; for the side view, look directly towards triangular face $AEB$.

answer.short: Plan: rectangle. Back: rectangle. Side: right-angled triangle.
answer.worked: From above, the projected footprint is a rectangle. Looking directly towards $BCDE$ gives a rectangle. Looking towards $AEB$ gives a right-angled triangle, with the vertical edge on the right as shown.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 1c; matched answer on teacher PDF page 66
spec.description: Three labelled orthographic views in one row, with a common baseline: square plan, rectangular back and triangular side.
spec.mathematics: Plan has equal footprint dimensions; back and side share the wedge height. Side has a right angle at its lower-right vertex.
